requiredFindings.title: Charge the native component-name copies and include them in all affected recipes
requiredFindings.finding: component() constructs a fresh CString, but open_regular_no_follow, entry_status, create_symlink and read_link charge only the native/status price and delegate copied-name accounting to callers. Most callers do not fund that copy. A root-level transfer is a minimal example: transfer_bound and the actual transfer charge zero objects, yet open_regular_no_follow allocates its basename CString before its own charge. V1/V2/open status reads and file opens, plus symlink basename copies, have the same omission. The target record does not fund the separate symlink basename. Thus exact object/byte equality in CI-T22 currently confirms an underpriced ledger, rather than complete work accounting. LAW item 4 explicitly prices copied native names as owned records; CI-A2 does not amend these omissions.
requiredFindings.requestedChange: Fund each actual name copy before allocation, or use a previously funded reusable/stack representation that avoids the allocation. State the ownership and NUL-byte convention explicitly, update the affected B_install/B_open/B_transfer rows and CI-A2 as needed, and independently verify allocations and refusal before an unfunded copy. Avoid double charging the existing generation-name, archive-path and descent records.

requiredFindings.title: Make CI-A2-e consistently amend LAW reservation semantics
requiredFindings.finding: CI-A2-e changes the admission sentence to reserve the whole transaction with effect/prepaid, while expressly saying nothing else changes. LAW line 212 still says only step 6 is reserved and every other row is executed and charged in its step. That is incompatible with install reserving the entire bound up front. The shortfall text also continues to name B_install instead of the proposed maximum. In addition, CI-A2-e describes the reinstall bound as the existence check and store custody, then B_open; B_open already contains store custody, whereas reinstall_bound correctly adds only the existence check/name to B_open. The amendment as written therefore describes a different custody count from the code.
requiredFindings.requestedChange: Quote and replace the reserved-versus-executed paragraph and affected shortfall/bound references as well as line 122. Explain the outer reservation, prepaid execution, nested publication reservation and single ledger debit. Define the reinstall bound with store custody exactly once, matching implementation and independent controls.

requiredFindings.title: Complete the promised independent operation and allocation controls
requiredFindings.finding: The implemented checks do not provide the full independent accounting evidence required by CI-T22/CI-PT-7. The B_open test compares used counters only to production open_bound; B_transfer likewise compares counters to production transfer_bound and checks the descent object count. Neither independently enumerates the complete operation recipe. CI-PT-7 independently counts comparator calls, which does catch comparison-after-charge, but observes no allocations: its short-scratch case only checks that no comparator ran. Moving Vec::with_capacity before its still-present charge can preserve every assertion while performing an unfunded allocation. The packaged scratch mutation deletes a charge, so it does not demonstrate allocation-before-charge detection. The required 100,000-entry handle-discipline control and per-entry-handle mutation are also explicitly unmeasured. These are acceptance-plan obligations, not merely an unreported performance benchmark.
requiredFindings.requestedChange: Add an independent operation/allocation oracle or sufficiently complete source-order guards with adversarial controls: enumerate B_open and B_transfer fixed rows independently; detect scratch allocation before its charge with the charge retained; and demonstrate bounded live handles on the specified large tree, catching a handle-per-entry implementation. Instrumentation may live in the platform test owner rather than adding unsafe code to lifecycle. Keep comparisons/read attempts as upper bounds and objects/bytes exact, including RF-1 corrections.

nonBlockingObservations.title: Keep the disclosed integration and fault-injection gaps explicit
nonBlockingObservations.observation: CI-T16 belongs to CI-4. The signed half of CI-T11 still needs profile-1 signed fixture integration; fixture/release symbol separation is already evidenced. Crashed-holder release and an injected parent-barrier failure remain unexercised; the inspected close-only pin and explicit uncertain-barrier route are consistent with their platform contracts. I do not add separate required findings for those four disclosed gaps in this library unit. They must not be reported as exercised, and this review accepts no CI-4 code or production qualification.
